RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The panel's composition alone proves little — economics departments are male-dominated, so all-male panels occur frequently by chance, and mixed panels show similar bias patterns in research. As standalone evidence it's weak.

Your stronger point is substantive: a completed PhD, six papers and four years' teaching versus an unfinished PhD and two papers. If "industry experience" wasn't weighted in the advertised criteria, that's a procedural problem regardless of sex.

So: pursue the written reasons first (they're likely legally owed to you — chase in writing, copy HR, cite any statutory deadline). Lead with the credential and criteria mismatch. Mention panel composition only as context if the explanation reveals vague or shifting justifications — not as your opening argument.
